Kody Guide: Usage and Configuration


Interacting with Kody

- **Request a Review:** Ask Kody to review your PR manually by adding a comment with the `@kody start-review` command at the root of your PR.

- **Validate Business Logic:** Ask Kody to validate your code against business rules by adding a comment with the `@kody -v business-logic` command.

- **Provide Feedback:** Help Kody learn and improve by reacting to its comments with a 👍 for helpful suggestions or a 👎 if improvements are needed.

`kody|code-review` `bug` `severity-level|medium`

**Math.floor truncates attendance ratio before multiplying by 100**

Truncating the ratio before multiplying by 100 returns 0 for any partial attendance, so every student fails the ≤75 check. Wrap the whole percentage in `Math.floor`, as in `Math.floor((a.present / a.total) * 100)`.

Was this suggestion helpful? Reply with 👍 or 👎 to help Kody learn from this interaction.

```
👍
```

```

```

`kody|code-review` **Prompt for LLM**: copy into your coding agent

```text
File src/qa2628r/attendance-rate.ts, line 5:

Math.floor truncates attendance ratio before multiplying by 100

`Math.floor` is applied to `present / total` before multiplying by 100, so the ratio is truncated to 0 or 1 and the function returns 0 for any partial attendance (e.g. 90/100 → 0). Every student then appears to fail the ≤75 check; the truncation must wrap the whole percentage: `Math.floor((a.present / a.total) * 100)`.

Suggested code:

return Math.floor((a.present / a.total) * 100);
```

`kody|code-review` `bug` `severity-level|medium`

**Division by zero in attendanceRate yields Infinity/NaN**

A student with no recorded classes silently passes, because the undefined ratio propagates into `failsByAbsence`, where `NaN <= 75` is false. Guard the empty case in `attendanceRate` and return 0 before dividing.

Was this suggestion helpful? Reply with 👍 or 👎 to help Kody learn from this interaction.

```
👍
```

```
👎
```

`kody|code-review` **Prompt for LLM**: copy into your coding agent

```text
File src/qa2628r/attendance-rate.ts, line 5:

Division by zero in attendanceRate yields Infinity/NaN

`a.total === 0` makes `a.present / a.total` produce `Infinity`/`NaN`, which propagates through `attendanceRate` into `failsByAbsence`, where `NaN <= 75` is `false` — a student with no recorded classes is silently treated as passing. Guard the empty case and return 0 before dividing.

Suggested code:

if (a.total === 0) return 0;
  return Math.floor(a.present / a.total) * 100;
```

`kody|code-review` `bug` `severity-level|high`

**Loop condition `i <= own.length` reads past end and throws on empty grades**

Reading `own[own.length]` is `undefined`, so `own[i].score` throws on every call, and a student with no grades crashes immediately. Change the bound to `i < own.length`.

```
👍
```

```
👎
```

`kody|code-review` **Prompt for LLM**: copy into your coding agent

```text
File src/qa2628r/grade-book.ts, lines 7-8:

Loop condition `i <= own.length` reads past end and throws on empty grades

The loop condition `i <= own.length` iterates once past the last element; `own[own.length]` is `undefined`, so `own[i].score` throws `TypeError` on every call. It also crashes immediately for a student with no grades (`own.length === 0`); the bound must be `i < own.length`.
```

`kody|code-review` `bug` `severity-level|medium`

**recoveryList returns students above passing mark instead of below**

The filter returns exactly the passing students and omits the ones needing recovery, contradicting the doc comment. Invert the comparison to `< passingMark`.

```text
File src/qa2628r/grade-book.ts, line 16:

recoveryList returns students above passing mark instead of below

The filter keeps students whose average is *greater* than `passingMark`, but the doc comment says students below the passing mark go to recovery, so the function returns exactly the passing students and omits the ones needing recovery. Invert the comparison to `< passingMark`.

Suggested code:

return ids.filter((id) => weightedAverage(grades, id) < passingMark);
```
